result: NO OBSERVED CROSS-VM MUTABLE CACHE PATH; ROOT CAUSE UNRESOLVED

source_findings.finding: Immutable runtime/ROM cache retains private byte copies. Memory hits return a slice; storage hits allocate a verified ArrayBuffer. Firmware/virtual Flash are not passed to this asset cache.
Compilation cache retains only WebAssembly.Module and a byte-length number, never an Instance, Memory, filesystem, eFuse or mutable Flash.

Each start awaits prior stop, advances generation, creates a new UUID/abort controller, normalizes full Flash into a new byte array, retains a separate saved copy and creates a fresh iframe/MessageChannel. Transfer includes immutable resource copies plus that new Flash, not a previous Memory.

Each dedicated engine imports a fresh blob factory, uses a new WebAssembly.Instance when compiled code is cached, writes fresh Flash/ROM/eFuse into the per-factory FS, and does not supply wasmMemory to the main factory.

Actual SHA-bound Emscripten factory allocates a new shared WebAssembly.Memory when main Module.wasmMemory is absent, and initializes its own FS/MEMFS. Pthreads share memory within one guest only. Existing code and compiled Module caching do not retain that guest Memory.

limits: No new guest/build was run for this audit.
No direct host object-identity instrumentation compared dead-realm HEAP objects; freshness is established from executed source structure and recorded lifecycle, not a cross-realm pointer measurement.
A cached compile changes startup duration and host scheduling. This audit does not exclude a timing-sensitive QEMU/WASM CPU bug or prove why the warm guest entered BREAK/RESET.
Factory cold run and warm failure are preserved separately; no retry replaced the failure.
